objectives.label: Found out what the forest was objecting to
Helped the unicorns mend a hurt glade

goal.text: Find out what the forest is counting, and why.

steps.label: Find what hurts the forest most

facet_glade.name: The Glade Stone
facet_glade.text: From the heart of the Woods' worst glade. Warm, loud, and no mosshorn will come near it.

scene_tree_line.narration: The Enchanted Woods begin all at once, like a wall somebody painted green. As you step under the first branches, a fern unrolls, looks you up and down, and rolls itself back up. Somewhere in here, something is counting, and it has just reached you. Every road north runs through these trees, so before you go any further, you need to find out what the forest is counting, and why.

choices.label: Walk in under the trees
Wait at the edge to be invited in
Come in through the southeastern glades, boots still dry
Squelch in along the flooded western paths

scene_tree_line_walk_in.narration: You just walk in, the plain way, under the first branches. A fern counts you. An acorn drops on the first head through, which is fairly clearly the forest's way of saying "one". Another acorn follows for every head after it, one each, counted. Then the whole forest goes quiet, the way a teacher goes quiet while writing something down.

choices.label: Follow the path in

scene_tree_line_wait.narration: You stop at the edge and wait, the way you would at a stranger's front door. Nothing happens for a while. Then the fern unrolls again, slowly, and bends right down into a low green bow, and the brambles across the path lift themselves aside like a curtain. The forest likes good manners. It is the sort of host that notices who wipes their feet.

choices.label: Step in, politely

scene_se_glades.narration: The southeastern glades are carpeted in bluebells that really do ring, very quietly, when a boot brushes them. You're early, you're dry, and everybody can still see Gullet waving her notched hat from the far bank. In a pocket you find a honeycake that Gullet must have slipped in when nobody was looking.

choices.label: Follow the ringing deeper in

scene_flooded_paths.narration: You come in late and dripping, along paths that are mostly puddle, under the green roofs near MossHome, the bigfoot town. Maybe you chose this forest. Maybe the river chose it for you. A MossHome flood-warden in very tall boots hands you a jar of mosslight and says, "Happens every season. Not usually to this many."

choices.label: Wring out and walk on

variants.text: For you, it was the river. The west branch swept you off the ford, away from all those waiting wagons, and through the marsh to here. Somewhere back east, the drovers are still singing the crossing verse without you.

scene_runner_path.narration: A bigfoot runner comes jogging down the path toward you, a bundle of knotted cords over one shoulder. Right in front of her, the path folds itself up like a napkin and is gone. She keeps jogging in place, frowning at the ferns. "Third time today," she puffs. "MossHome runner. Bigfoot town, up north. Can't stop. Never stop. Can't get through, either."

choices.label: Help her find where the path went
Offer to carry a bundle of cords for her
Knock on a trunk and jog with her, the MossHome way

check_runner_path.prompt: Work out where a folded-up path has gone

onSuccess.narration: All the ferns along one side are leaning the same way, like people pointing. You follow them, and there's the path, only a little way over, sulking behind a holly bush. The runner whoops. "MossHome is north!" she calls, jogging off. "Come and see us! Bring your feet!"

onFailure.narration: You find a path. It is the wrong one, and it walks you in a neat circle back to the runner, who has found the right one herself while you were gone and is jogging in place, laughing. "Happens to everybody this season," she puffs, and jogs away north.

scene_runner_path_carry.narration: You take a bundle of cords. It's heavier than it looks. Every knot, she puffs, is a path that has moved since the mountain went off. "Archivists are tying the whole forest up in knots. Running out of cord." At the next bend the path unfolds for her at once. "Forest likes records," she says, takes the bundle back, and jogs off north.

choices.label: Walk on, arms aching

scene_runner_path_knock.narration: Your bigfoot knocks on a trunk, two slow knocks, and jogs alongside her, easy and steady. The folded path shakes itself out like a blanket and lies back down where it belongs. The runner grins all over her face. "Haven't seen a knock like that outside town," she puffs. "MossHome's north. Come and visit." And she is gone.

choices.label: Walk on, knuckles proud

scene_roll_call.narration: The path opens into a round clearing ringed by tall trees. As you step in, the leaves begin to rustle in turn, one tree after another, slow as a teacher taking attendance. They are calling names. A squirrel answers "Here!" and scampers off. A prospector answers, and the path behind him quietly shuts. Now the rustling is coming around to you.

choices.label: Answer "Here!" nice and loud
Answer by saying out loud everything you carry
Let Mother Thrum's tuned charm answer for you

variants.text: It slows right down over Mother Thrum's tuned charm from the ford, and the charm gives one small chime back, like a hand going up.
It gives your brave whistle a short, approving rustle, the way you would nod at somebody wearing a medal.
Over the curl of cold silver from the marsh, it goes very quiet, and then hurries on, the way you skip a page you are not ready to read.
It counts your jar of mosslight, and the jar glows a little brighter, as if it likes being counted.
The Barge Stone from the marsh gets the longest rustle of all.
The Ford Stone from the river crossing gets the longest rustle of all.

scene_roll_call_here.narration: "Here!" you shout. The trees rustle, satisfied. Then the rustling carries on, slowly, as if it is reading out what is in your packs: socks, crumbs, a spoon, a cookie you forgot about. Anything that hums gets a long, thoughtful rustle all of its own. At last, with the air of a teacher closing a book, a path opens.

choices.label: Walk on, feeling counted

check_roll_call_truth.prompt: Name everything you carry, honestly, even the embarrassing bits

onSuccess.narration: You empty your pockets onto a stump and name everything out loud, even the squashed cookie, even the stone if you have one. The trees rustle warmly, the way grown-ups do when you own up first. A path opens, wide and sunny, and the forest seems to make a little note about you.

onFailure.narration: You name everything, very honestly, and then a frog climbs out of somebody's hood. Nobody knew it was there. It has been there since the river. The trees rustle about this for a long time, and you are fairly sure they are laughing. The frog hops off. A path opens, eventually.

scene_roll_call_charm.narration: You hold up the witch's tuned charm, and it rings all by itself, the note the stones hum. The clearing goes silent. Then, very faintly, every tree rings back the same note, like a room of people humming a tune they all learned long ago. The forest knows that note. A path opens, quietly, and the charm stops ringing.

choices.label: Walk on, the charm warm in your hand

scene_attendance.narration: Deeper in, the paths start doing something strange. One opens in front of you like a door. Another closes behind a gang of prospectors with bulging pockets, and they walk straight into a hedge that wasn't there a second ago. The forest isn't checking who you are. It's checking what you carry.

choices.label: Take the path that opens for you
Ask the trees, politely, what they're counting
The Barge Stone hums, and a path slams shut. Ask why.

scene_attendance_open_path.narration: You take the path that opens for you. It closes neatly behind you, like a door held by a very good butler, and the next one opens just ahead. It is a bit like being passed from hand to hand. Then, around a bend, you hear somebody shouting at a hedge. The hedge does not seem to be listening.

choices.label: Go and see

check_ask_trees.prompt: Ask the forest, politely, what it is objecting to

onSuccess.narration: Something tall creaks, and leans, and leans some more, until it's close enough to whisper.

onFailure.narration: The trees rustle something long and complicated. It might be an answer. It might be a soup recipe. You walk past the same embarrassed toadstool three times before a path lets you through, and on the far side somebody is shouting at a hedge.

scene_forest_objects.narration: An old beech tree has bent right down to whisper, and it smells of rain. It is not you the forest minds, it says. It is the stones, and what they did to the places where they fell. Where a stone landed, the glade around it is hurting. Pocket one, and the forest shuts its doors on you, just in case.

choices.label: Thank the beech and walk on

scene_hedge.narration: The prospectors who walked into the hedge are still in it. Not stuck, exactly. Held. The hedge has them by the coat-tails, very gently, and every time one wriggles it rustles "tsk". Their pockets bulge and hum. "Let us out!" shouts the biggest. "We only took what fell!" The hedge does not let go. And nobody gets left in a hedge.

choices.label: Pull them out by the boots
Tell them to empty their pockets
Lower your horn and ask the hedge, quietly, what it wants

check_hedge_pull.prompt: Pull three prospectors out of a hedge that doesn't want to let go

onSuccess.narration: You grab a boot each and heave. Out they pop like corks, one, two, three. But their coats stay in the hedge, and so does everything in the pockets. The gems sink into the leaves, humming, and are gone. The prospectors pat their shirts, then stare at the hedge, then run.

onFailure.narration: You heave. The hedge heaves back, and now it is holding your sleeves too. In a panic, the biggest prospector empties his pockets on the ground, and the moment the gems touch the moss, roots curl around them and pull them under. The hedge lets everybody go at once, as if nothing happened.

scene_hedge_empty.narration: "It isn't you it wants," you tell them. "It's what you're carrying." They grumble. They argue. Then, one by one, they turn out their pockets. The gems roll into the moss, and roots curl around them like fingers and draw them down. The hedge lets go at once. The prospectors stare at the ground. "It's taking them," one whispers. "Where's it taking them?"

choices.label: Walk on, wondering the same thing

scene_hedge_ask.narration: You lower your horn to the hedge and ask. The leaves stop rustling. In the hush you feel the answer, the way you feel warm or cold: not them, never them, only the stones. Very slowly the hedge opens its hands. The gems drop out of the prospectors' pockets into the moss and sink away, and the prospectors, freed, bow to you, confused.

choices.label: Walk on, knowing

scene_mosshorns.narration: A herd of mosshorns grazes ahead, their antlers sprouting little gardens. One has a whole strawberry patch on its head and is clearly very proud of it. A prospector's cart rattles by with a sack of gems, and the entire herd steps away from it at once, like one long breath out.

choices.label: Read the herd
Sit very still and watch them
Walk on past the herd

scene_mosshorns_walk_on.narration: You walk on past the herd, keeping well back. The mosshorn with the strawberry patch watches you go, chewing. It steps a long way away from the prospector's cart, and only a little way from you, and then goes back to its strawberries. A little further on, the moss under your feet turns gray.

choices.label: Look down

check_watch_herd.prompt: Watch the herd long enough to see the pattern

onSuccess.narration: You sit so still a beetle walks across your boot. And then you see it.

onFailure.narration: A mosshorn wanders over, inspects you thoroughly, sneezes on you, and leaves. That, apparently, was the whole conversation. You walk on, and soon your boots find a bare gray patch where nothing grows at all.

scene_read_herd.narration: The mosshorns don't mind people. They mind the stones. They walk wide around anything that hums, and they will not graze where a stone has fallen. You can see the bald gray patches in the forest where they have stopped going. The herd is a map of where it hurts.

choices.label: Follow the gray patches

scene_gray_patch.narration: In a bald gray patch, where nothing grows and no mosshorn will graze, a crumb of fallen stone glitters in the moss. It's no bigger than a pea, and it is humming, very small and very determined, like a bee in a jar. Around it the moss has gone gray in a perfect ring. A beetle walks the long way around.

choices.label: Pocket it. It's tiny.
Press it gently down into the moss

scene_gray_patch_pocket.narration: You pick up the crumb. Ten steps ahead, the path you were about to take folds itself shut. Another one closes to your left. Then another. You look at the crumb. You put it back down. Every path opens again at once, like held breath let out. Well. Now you know exactly what the forest minds.

choices.label: Leave the crumb where it fell

check_gray_patch_press.prompt: Press the humming crumb down into the moss, gently, the way you'd tuck in a blanket

onSuccess.narration: You press it down, gently, and the moss takes it like a pocket closing. The hum goes muffled, then quiet. And right in the middle of the gray ring, one bright green shoot pokes up and unrolls. A very small mend. Somebody nearby, with ears, has noticed.

onFailure.narration: You press it down. It pops back up. You press it again. It pops up again, like a cork in a bath. On the third try you give up and plant a stick beside it as a flag, so whoever mends these things can find it. Somebody nearby, with ears, has noticed that too.

scene_unicorns.narration: In a small glade the moss has gone the color of cold porridge, and every flower is facing the wrong way. Two unicorns stand in it, horns lowered, frowning the way unicorns frown, which is mostly with the ears. "A stone fell here," says the older one. "We are mending. Will you help?"

choices.label: Help them mend the glade
Keep watch at the glade edge while they work
Lay your horn on the bruise
Tell them about the patch you greened

scene_unicorns_horn.narration: You lower your horn to the bruise beside the two unicorns. It feels like pressing on a sore knee, and then like the knee feeling better. Green creeps out from under your horn in a slow ring, and the flowers turn around to see who did it. The elder unicorn's ears tip forward. For a unicorn, that is a standing ovation.

choices.label: Lift your horn

scene_unicorns_guard.narration: You stand guard at the edge of the glade while the unicorns mend, horns low, humming. Nothing comes. A mosshorn peers in, sees you guarding, and backs out again, very respectfully. A squirrel tries to cross and you make it wait. By the time you turn around, the moss is green again, and the elder unicorn nods: a good guard is help too.

choices.label: Go back to the unicorns

scene_unicorns_patch.narration: You tell them about the crumb you pressed down and the green shoot. The elder unicorn's ears go straight up. "Down," she says. "Not away. Down." She steps aside and lets you start the mending hum, and the unicorns join in under you, low and steady. The cold-porridge moss turns green from the middle out.

choices.label: Let the hum fade

check_mend.prompt: Hum with the unicorns, hands flat on the moss, while it remembers its color

onSuccess.narration: Green creeps back from the middle, like a spill going backwards. The flowers turn around one by one to face the sun.

onFailure.narration: You hum, and the moss goes green, then gray, then a sort of hopeful beige. The unicorns finish it themselves, very kindly, while you hold their saddlebags.

scene_finding.narration: When the glade is quiet, the older unicorn rests her horn on the spot where the stone fell. "These stones are not of the mountain," she says. "The forest remembers them. It remembers them from before the mountain had its name." She says nothing else about that, and somehow that makes it louder. Then, quieter: "This was a small one. The worst glade is north of here. We have not managed that one yet."

choices.label: Ask what she means, before the mountain had its name
Ask how to mend the worst glade
Say nothing, and sit down at the glade's edge

scene_finding_before.narration: You ask what she means. The elder unicorn has already said the important thing, and unicorns say important things once. Her ears frown. The younger unicorn leans over and whispers instead: "She means old. Older than names. She won't say it twice." A pause. "She didn't much like saying it once."

choices.label: Sit down at the glade's edge

scene_finding_how.narration: "Slowly," says the elder unicorn. "The forest dislikes hurry. And something lives in the worst glade now that listens for loud things. Go quiet, or go so noisy it can't follow." She looks at your packs for a long moment, then away, as if she has decided to trust you. That is a lot of words, for her. She looks tired.

choices.label: Sit down at the glade's edge

scene_finding_rest.narration: You say nothing at all, and just sit down at the edge of the mended glade. The elder unicorn looks at you sideways, and then, for the first time, she smiles. Unicorns like very much to be left alone with a good silence. The younger one lies down next to you, and the moss under you goes soft as a pillow.

choices.label: Settle in

rest_glade_edge.narration: You rest where the moss is soft again. A mosshorn calf wanders over and falls asleep across everybody's feet, and nobody is allowed to move until it wakes up. Those are the rules. Everyone knows the rules.

choices.label: Slide out from under the calf and go on
Hum the calf a lullaby first

rest_glade_edge_on.narration: You slide out from under the calf as gently as anything. It wakes anyway, blinks, sneezes, and gets up on legs much too long for it. When you set off toward the worst glade, it comes too, wobbling along behind you and stopping to eat a flower every few steps. Nobody has the heart to send it back.

choices.label: Walk on, with company

rest_glade_edge_lullaby.narration: You hum, soft and low. The calf snores in time. The unicorns hum too, under you, and for a while the whole glade hums along. When at last the calf wakes, it gets up, licks everybody's boots one after the other, very thoroughly, and decides you are its herd now. It follows you out of the glade, proud as a drum major.

choices.label: Walk on, with company

scene_lost_calf.narration: Halfway to the worst glade, the calf is still following you, all knees and antler buds, with one daisy growing between its ears. Its herd is nowhere to be seen, and a calf this small should not be this far from its mother. It looks up at you as if you are the herd now. Then it sneezes, and the daisy wobbles.

choices.label: Call the herd the way mosshorns call
Carry it back the way you came
Let the calf lead you to its herd

check_calf_call.prompt: Hoot like a mosshorn, long and low, so the herd comes for its calf

onSuccess.narration: You hoot, long and low. Far off, something hoots back. Out of the trees comes the strawberry-patch mosshorn and the whole herd behind it. The calf trots home, and the big mosshorn lowers its whole garden of antlers to you, very slowly, which is how mosshorns say thank you.

onFailure.narration: Your hoot comes out like a goose with hiccups. The calf looks at you, embarrassed on your behalf, and hoots properly itself. The herd answers at once and comes to fetch it. As it trots home, the calf looks back at you with deep pity. You have been out-hooted by a baby.

scene_lost_calf_carry.narration: You carry the calf back the way you came. It is heavier than it looks, and it eats a little of your hair on the way. At the glade's edge, the herd is waiting. The calf's mother takes it back with a sniff that says "and where have YOU been", and then she lowers her antlers to you, slowly. Mosshorns remember.

choices.label: Walk back toward the worst glade

scene_lost_calf_lead.narration: The calf trusts you, so you trust it. It leads you down a mosshorn path you would never have found, under ferns taller than you, and straight into the middle of its herd. The big mosshorns crowd around, sniffing your lullaby-hummed boots. Then the whole herd walks you to the last stretch before the worst glade, like an escort.

choices.label: Thank the herd and walk on

scene_sitting_beech.narration: On the last stretch to the worst glade, a huge beech, fatter and mossier than any tree you have passed, has sat down across the path like a grandpa in an armchair, roots tucked under, with a beard of gray lichen. "Before you see the worst of it," it whispers, very slowly, "tell me why you came." A squirrel on its shoulder taps one foot, impatiently. What do you tell it? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Tell it the truth: the stones
Say you're just passing through
Say you came to find out what is really going on
Remind it you told the roll call everything

scene_sitting_beech_stones.narration: "The stones," you say. The beech is quiet for so long that the squirrel falls asleep. "Honest," it whispers at last. "Most say they are just passing through." Creak by creak, it stands up and shuffles aside. "Go gently," it says. "The glade is very sore. And something down there is listening."

choices.label: Go gently

scene_sitting_beech_passing.narration: "Passing through," the beech repeats, very slowly. "Everybody is passing through. Even me. I am just slower about it." It gets up one root at a time, which takes long enough to eat a whole cookie. Then it waves you on with a branch, not at all convinced, but far too polite to say so.

choices.label: Pass through

scene_sitting_beech_curious.narration: "To find out," the beech repeats, and every leaf on it rustles at once, pleased. "Curious. Good. The forest has been waiting for somebody curious." It stands up quite fast, for a beech, and on the way past it drops a leaf on your shoulder, as if to say: look closely in there. Look at everything.

choices.label: Go and look

scene_sitting_beech_told.narration: "You told the roll call everything," you remind it. "Even the cookie." The beech creaks with what is definitely laughter. "I know," it whispers. "The whole forest knows. I was only being polite." It gets up at once, the squirrel clinging on, and bows you past. You have never been bowed at by a tree before.

choices.label: Walk on, bowed at

scene_crater.narration: The worst glade is a hollow torn into the forest floor where a big stone landed, and the crash cracked the ground open into the dark. Something pale and frilled has climbed up out of the crack. It has no eyes at all, and it is listening very hard to the humming in the middle of the glade. Now it is listening to you.

choices.label: Make the dark noisy: clap, stamp, shout
Tiptoe past without a sound
Knock on a tree and walk in slow and steady
Look back. The mosshorn herd has followed you.
Stand your ground

scene_crater_steady.narration: Your bigfoot knocks on a tree, three slow knocks, and walks into the glade slow and steady, the way bigfoot walk through MossHome at night. Everybody follows in step. The echo hunter tilts its frilled head. A sound that steady is not interesting at all. It yawns, a pale, silent yawn, and slides back down its crack.

choices.label: Walk to the middle of the glade

scene_crater_herd.narration: The mosshorn herd has followed you, at a distance. Not one hoof steps onto the gray. But at the glade's edge they stamp, all together, a great soft drumming that fills the hollow with sound from every side. The echo hunter's frills flatten. Far too much to listen to. It slides back into its crack to wait for some peace.

choices.label: Thank the herd and walk in

check_noisy.prompt: Make so many sounds at once that the echo hunter can't follow any of them

onSuccess.narration: Clapping, stamping, a pot lid, somebody yodeling. The echo hunter's frills flatten in dismay, and it backs down its crack to wait for some peace and quiet.

onFailure.narration: You manage one sound, very loudly, over and over. That is exactly the kind it likes.

check_silent.prompt: Cross the glade without making a single sound

onSuccess.narration: Not a twig. Not a breath. The hunter tilts its head, puzzled, and hears nothing at all.

onFailure.narration: A twig. A snap. A pale head turns.

encounter_echo.narration: The echo hunter comes up out of its crack, frills spread wide. It is a young one, not much bigger than a pony. A wisp drawn by the stone's hum drifts down to join in.

onVictory.narration: The hunter decides you are far too loud to be worth it and slides back down into the dark. The wisp loses interest and drifts off to bother a mosshorn.

onDefeat.narration: The echo hunter herds you out of the glade, nudge by patient nudge, all the way to a path that closes neatly behind you. When you turn around, the glade is gone.

check_way_back.prompt: Find the hidden way back to the worst glade

onSuccess.narration: You follow the gray patches the mosshorns won't graze, and they lead you straight back. Late and scuffed, but there.

onFailure.narration: The gray patches lead you in a circle, and then into a hedge, and then past an embarrassed-looking toadstool, twice. The forest has decided where you are going, and it is not the glade.

scene_glade_heart.narration: In the very middle of the worst glade, in a bruise of gray moss, sits a gem the size of a fist, humming. Every tree leans away from it. Two unicorns watch from the edge. So, very quietly, does the forest. Mend the glade, and the stone sinks back into the ground where the forest keeps it. Take the stone, and this glade will never mend. Everybody vote.

choices.label: Mend the glade and let the stone go
Pocket the stone

scene_mend_glade.narration: You kneel around the stone and press it, gently, down into the moss. It sinks like a pebble into honey. Green spreads out from the middle in a ring, and every flower in the glade turns around at once to look at you. The unicorns bow, ears and all.

choices.label: Walk on, lighter

scene_pocket_stone.narration: The Glade Stone is warm in your hand and loud in your pocket. Behind you, the glade goes quiet, the way a room goes quiet when somebody says the wrong thing. The unicorns don't say a word. One of them writes something down.

choices.label: Walk on, quickly

scene_pile_shown.narration: On the way out, a path opens that was not there before and leads you past an enormous hollow oak. Inside, piled to the roof: pickaxes, panniers, a prospector's hat with a feather in it, and gems, dozens of them, humming together like a choir. The forest has been confiscating. It shows you, the way a friend shows you a secret drawer, and then the bark closes over it like a lid.

choices.label: Keep the secret, and head north
Ask the oak what it's keeping them for

scene_pile_shown_on.narration: You say nothing, and the oak says nothing back, which between people and trees is a promise. All the way north, every path opens a moment before you reach it, like doors held by a very good host. Once, a branch lifts itself out of the way of a tall head. Nobody had to duck at all.

choices.label: Out to the forest edge

scene_pile_shown_ask.narration: You ask. The oak creaks, and the smell of rain drifts by. The answer comes in creaks and drips, slow as sap: until somebody comes who can be trusted with them. The bigfoot keep the record. Ask at MossHome. Then the bark settles over the hole, and a path opens north, toward MossHome.

choices.label: Head for MossHome

scene_pile_glimpsed.narration: The paths close around you one by one, until the only way left squeezes past an enormous hollow oak. For just a moment you see inside: pickaxes, panniers, a feathered hat, and gems, dozens of them, humming. The forest has been confiscating. A root slides across the hole like a lid, and a branch gives your pocket a long, meaningful look.

choices.label: Hurry north
Tell the oak you're sorry, but you're keeping it

scene_pile_glimpsed_on.narration: You hurry. Paths open for you, but only just, and only at the very last moment, like a door held by somebody who hasn't decided whether to slam it. The Glade Stone hums the whole way, extremely pleased with itself. You are a good deal less pleased. A bramble catches your sleeve, twice, on purpose.

choices.label: Out to the forest edge

scene_pile_glimpsed_sorry.narration: "Sorry," you tell the oak. "We're keeping it." The root stays across the hole. There is a long creak, like somebody thinking it over. Then one leaf drifts down and lands on your pocket, right over the stone, like a label. The forest has written your name next to the Glade Stone. It will remember who has it.

choices.label: Walk north, labeled

ending_marked_present.narration: You camp at the northern edge of the Woods on moss as soft as a pillow. Just before dark, the MossHome runner jogs by on a path that stays put for once. "MossHome's just north!" she puffs, and does not stop. All night, a mosshorn stands at the edge of your firelight like a guard, its antler flowers open. The forest has taken attendance, and it has marked you present.

ending_marked_something.narration: You camp at the northern edge of the Woods, where the paths finally let you out. Just before dark, the MossHome runner jogs by on a path that stays put for once. "MossHome's just north!" she puffs, and does not stop. The Glade Stone hums in your pack all night. No mosshorns come anywhere near. The forest has taken attendance, and next to your name it has written something you can't quite read.

ending_shown_the_door.narration: By the time you find your way back, the worst glade is already green. The unicorns mended it without you, and the stone has sunk back into the ground where nobody will ever pocket it. The forest walks you to its northern edge, politely, the way you walk a guest to the door. Just before dark, the MossHome runner jogs by and waves. "MossHome's just north!" she puffs. Camp at the edge of the trees, scuffed and a little sorry.

voiceGuide.tone: green, hushed and watchful; the forest is a polite host keeping a ledger, a little spooky but never scary
forbidden: explaining what the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.beech_tree: old, slow, smells of rain; whispers in long sentences and never raises its voice
npcVoices.elder_unicorn: calm, few words, frowns with her ears; says the important thing once and stops
npcVoices.flood_warden: MossHome bigfoot in very tall boots; brisk, practical, has seen every kind of soggy
npcVoices.echo_hunter: never speaks; tilts its frilled head, listening, filing every sound
npcVoices.runner: a MossHome runner; cheerful, out of breath, never stops jogging even while talking, carries bundles of knotted cords
npcVoices.hedge_prospectors: prospectors held by a hedge; loud, indignant, then sheepish once their pockets are empty
